title: The Builder
eyebrow: CETI · a data film · the best builder does not make the best agent
lede: 320 customer cases, six agent builds each: 1,920 tries, 968 lit. Sorted by how many builds solved each case, the columns climb a staircase with 44 dark columns at one end and 43 full ones at the other, five times what luck leaves. The case decides more than the build; and an expert scores 82.2 where the best builder scores 23.9.
captions: The best builder makes the best agent.
Does it? Test it on real customer cases.
Airline, shop and phone-line customer cases.
320 cases. One tile each.
Six agent builds tried every case.
1,920 tries. One cube each.
A lit cube is a try that passed.
968 cubes are lit.
About half of the tries pass: 50.4 %.
Now turn the field. Each case becomes a column.
A column is one case, tried six ways.
Six different builds, not six repeats of one.
Look for columns that are all dark or all lit.
Sort the cases by how many builds solved them.
44 cases: no build solved them.
43 cases: every build solved them.
Now scatter the same wins at random.
Luck would leave 8.8 dark and 8.4 full.
Cut at six of six: 43 of 320 cases.
Only 13.4 % of cases are solved by all six.
Phone lines, regrouped by build.
Six builds: from 26.1 % to 52.1 %.
By kind of problem: 11.6 % to 67.7 %.
So the case matters more than the build.
Now the score: 53 tasks, four businesses.
The best builder scores 23.9 out of 100.
An expert who knows the test scores 82.2.
In banking: 5.9 against 79.8.
Last: what the builders asked the client.
15,885 tool calls. One cube each.
43 were questions to the client.

brand.takeaway: Ask the client. Test on the hard cases.

sources: https://github.com/sierra-research/hyper-tau-bench (commit 6e9f34c685d40fa7a9f5935d8970af6fd9d5f118, 2026-09-06) · web/leaderboard/public/hyper-submissions/*/submission.json (six configurations x four domains) and reference.json (the expert row); recomputed by factory/topics/reliability-data/recompute.py section 1; grade A

https://github.com/sierra-research/hyper-tau-bench (same commit) · web/leaderboard/public/build-trajectories/rel001..053.json: one sampled build per task, the 0/1 reward of every evaluation simulation, tool calls, messages to the Client; recomputed by data/recompute.py from data/hyper-tau-{matrix,builds,summary}.json; grade A
https://github.com/sierra-research/hyper-tau-bench (same commit) · data/tau2/hyper/tasks/MANIFEST.md: 53 tasks = 6 airline_plus + 6 retail_plus + 6 telecom + 35 banking_knowledge; grade A

https://github.com/sierra-research/hyper-tau-bench (same commit) · src/tau2/hyper/sandbox/orchestrator.py and performance.py: reward = max(0, pass rate - credit overage) x latency gate; board overall = mean over the 53 tasks; grade A

https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04611 · Shi, Dhandhania, Narasimhan, Barres (Sierra), 2026-09-04, the benchmark paper; abstract read through search-result text (grade B); NOT a source of any number on stage

factory/topics/build-the-agent/data/recompute.py · this topic's recompute (reads the three JSON copies); copies verified byte-identical to factory/topics/reliability-data/; upstream script reads the clone
honest: One sampled build per task, builders mixed: columns are different builds, not repeats; 23.9 is a mean over 53 tasks scored by simulated customers and an LLM judge.
